decisive_items: Lumbar puncture yielded an opening pressure of 23 cm H₂O and slightly hazy cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) with 538 WBCs/mm³
Repeat lumbar puncture showed an opening pressure of 30 cm H₂O, 1762 WBCs/mm³

Brain MRI revealed T2/FLAIR hyperintensity in the right basal ganglia and internal capsule with mild surrounding edema, scattered small foci of restricted diffusion, and subtle punctate blooming on susceptibility-weighted images
response.rationale: The patient's CSF findings, clinical presentation, and imaging results are most consistent with a pyogenic brain abscess, despite the negative Gram stain. The high WBC count in the CSF and the progression of symptoms support this diagnosis. While the patient's imaging findings could also suggest progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML), the negative John Cunningham virus PCR result reduces the likelihood of this diagnosis.

rejected.why: The absence of valvular vegetations on echocardiography reduces the likelihood of subacute bacterial endocarditis.
The negative rickettsial studies make this diagnosis less likely.

The lack of enhancement on MRI and the clinical context make this diagnosis less likely.
